lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Put the experience entries in reverse chronological order, with Lumen above the university role.
items.because: Lumen has the later end date.

items.says: Use one date style throughout the résumé.
items.because: The date formatting should have consistent punctuation and dash characters.

items.says: Verify the dates against the résumé’s submission date.
Test whether the pipe-separated headings and links parse correctly in the final PDF.
items.because: Text extraction or an ATS checker can reveal parsing problems.

items.says: Replace the placeholder contact details if they are not anonymized for review.
Label the code link or use a recognizable GitHub or portfolio URL.
items.because: Recruiters should immediately know what the link contains.

items.says: Make the email address and URL clickable in the PDF.
Consider adding a current city or work-location preference.
items.because: It may matter for the job search.

items.says: Make the expected graduation status visually unambiguous.
Consider reducing the repeated institution and location information if space is tight.
items.because: Compression should not sacrifice clarity.

items.says: Clarify whether the web developer role was full-time, part-time, contract, or student employment.
items.because: The employment arrangement could otherwise be unclear.

items.says: Replace or clarify “owned.”
items.because: It is vague and can imply authority beyond the actual role.

items.says: Add the scope of the websites and component library.
items.because: Numbers of sites, components, developers, departments, or users would show the scale.

items.says: Include an outcome if possible.
items.because: The bullet is responsibility-focused while the other bullets are results-focused.

items.says: Clarify the role in designing and implementing preview mode.
items.because: The sentence jumps from research findings to the feature.

items.says: Define “broken pages reported.”
items.because: The count may include several types of incidents.

items.says: Check that the before-and-after incident counts cover comparable periods.
items.because: The reduction should be defensible in an interview.

items.says: Clarify what “12 to 2” counts.
items.because: Failed audits, failed pages, and failed checks are materially different.

items.says: Clarify what work connected the checklist to the reduction.
items.because: Writing a checklist alone should not be implied to have caused it.

items.says: Name the accessibility standard if applicable.
Define “search time.”
items.because: It could mean query latency, page-load time, or time needed to find a course.

items.says: Add the dataset’s scale.
items.because: It would show whether client-side filtering was technically meaningful.

items.says: Mention the relevant technology if it adds new information.
Name the exact performance metric behind the 35% improvement.
items.because: A percentage without a named metric is difficult to evaluate.

items.says: State how performance was measured if space permits.
items.because: The result may come from lab tooling rather than production data.

items.says: Clarify the level of ownership of the code splitting.
items.because: It is unclear whether it was implemented independently or contributed to.

items.says: Name the accessibility standard, audit tool, or validation process if accurate.
Verify that “all 14” issues were independently retested.
items.because: Otherwise the claim may overstate what was fixed.

items.says: Clarify the scope of the date-picker accessibility work if it already had partial support.
items.because: The bullet should not overstate building accessibility from scratch.

items.says: Add the test framework if it is relevant and was genuinely used.
Specify when the regressions were caught.
items.because: They could have been caught before merge, before deployment, or during a release cycle.

items.says: Consider emphasizing coverage or critical behaviors over the count of tests.
items.because: Those may be more meaningful if the tests were very small.

items.says: Lazy-loading the above-the-fold hero image is a technically inaccurate explanation for improving LCP.
items.because: It generally delays discovery and download of the LCP image.

items.says: Recheck the implementation, test conditions, and cause of the LCP improvement.
items.because: The 4.1s-to-1.2s result should be consistently measured and technically explainable.

items.says: Storing input in React state before rendering with dangerouslySetInnerHTML does not prevent XSS.
items.because: State does not sanitize input, and dangerouslySetInnerHTML bypasses React’s default escaping.

items.says: Explain the actual XSS control, threat model, and validation approach if retaining the claim.
items.because: An XSS-prevention claim needs a real control that can be explained in an interview.

items.says: Move the hotel-search result to the first or second Lumen bullet.
items.because: It combines substantial technical scope, performance improvement, and business impact.

items.says: Clarify whether the 9% booking improvement is relative or absolute.
State the ownership level if “rebuilt” overstates a team effort.
Consider naming the SSR framework if relevant and accurate.
Add a repository or live-product link if the header link does not lead directly to the project.
Include other central technologies if they were used substantially and strengthen the candidacy.
Clarify how weekly riders were measured.
items.because: The number should be credible.

items.says: Verify that “live” accurately describes the arrival data.
items.because: The data may instead be predictions or periodically refreshed.

items.says: Replace “against” with a clearer comparison construction.
State how the slow-3G measurement was produced if it was simulated.
Clarify whether 0.8s refers to first load, repeat load, or offline launch.
items.because: Caching affects those scenarios differently.

items.says: Add the repository link and any objective open-source adoption information.
Clarify whether the agency link drove usage if that connection can be supported.
The Vue heading contradicts the React and TypeScript project bullet.
items.because: The project technologies do not match across the entry.

items.says: List only technologies actually used in the project.
Verify the hackathon dates or clarify the event’s duration.
items.because: A two-month hackathon may raise questions unless it was an extended event.

items.says: The React and TypeScript claim conflicts with the project heading’s Vue listing.
items.because: The entry gives inconsistent technologies for the same project.

items.says: Replace “worked on” with the specific ownership and contribution.
items.because: The framing is weak.

items.says: Add a result, user flow, or delivered scope.
items.because: The bullet says little beyond participation.

items.says: Avoid repeating technologies if they are listed accurately in the project heading.
Add the testing framework if useful.
Clarify what the calendar did when booking conflicts occurred.
Keep “time-zone” from splitting awkwardly in the final PDF.
The travel-search accomplishment duplicates the Lumen result.
items.because: The same accomplishment should not appear in two sections.

items.says: The travel-search bullet appears unrelated to Library Room Booking.
items.because: It describes travel search rather than room booking.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled.
items.because: It should be “Storybook.”

items.says: Replace or split the “Tools” category.
items.because: It mixes a programming language, frameworks or libraries, and a development tool.

items.says: Consider adding core web technologies and the test framework if genuinely used.
Replace the vague “Methods” category name.
items.because: A different category could describe these competencies more accurately.

items.says: Make accessibility more specific.
items.because: Relevant standards and testing approaches would clarify the competency.

items.says: List testing tools rather than only “component testing.”
items.because: The phrase is broad.
